# Jamboree TV - Super Mario Party Jamboree - Mario Party Legacy
URL: https://mariopartylegacy.com/games/super-mario-party-jamboree/jamboree-tv/

Jamboree TV - Super Mario Party Jamboree - Mario Party Legacy

# Super Mario Party Jamboree – Jamboree TV

Jamboree TV is an upgrade pack for Super Mario Party Jamboree exclusively available for the Nintendo Switch 2 Edition of the game. It was released on July 24, 2025, and included new modes and a total of 20 new minigames that make use of the new console’s microphone, camera, and mouse capabilities.

You would think trying to explain post-launch content for a Mario Party game — a first for the series — would be easier, but here we are. Yes, the Jamboree got DLC and new content, but not everyone has access to it. Yes, there are new minigames, but some have accessory requirements. Yes, it is paid content, but it depends on what you already own. Lots of questions, so let’s break it all down.

Super Mario Party Jamboree – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV (yes, that’s the full title) was announced during the big Nintendo Switch 2 Direct. The plus sign adorned within the title is justified in this Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive game as Jamboree TV is an entirely separate game rather than content added to the base game. Once you boot it up, you’ll have the option to pick between the original Super Mario Party Jamboree game, the new Jamboree TV game, and the GameShare option. Think Super Mario 3D World + Bowser’s Fury and how that game separates the two right at the title screen!

Hop into Jamboree TV to find Toad hosting a game show. After all players select their characters, Yellow Toad, along with the newly added Talking Flowers from Super Mario Bros. Wonder, will present four stages to pick from. They include the camera-focused Bowser Live, the mouse-centric Carnival Coaster, an altered Mario Party mode, and a modified Free Play mode featuring most of the new minigames and a majority of the base game’s minigames.

 

Does Jamboree TV add any new characters or boards? Nope. We’ll detail the new features when breaking down each of the four stages, but don’t expect any new characters or boards.

- Bowser Live
- Carnival Coaster
- Mario Party
- Free Play (List of Minigames)

## Bowser Live

Bowser Live is the first of four modes in Jamboree TV. Once you boot up the mode, you’ll be asked to play between two different minigame types: camera and microphone. Each mode plays out the same way, but the minigames you play and the accessories needed are different.

 

Each game starts with two teams of two playing two minigames selected by a roulette. There are only three minigames in each type, so there will always be one that you don’t play. Your performance during the minigames will be tallied and the team with the most points by the end wins. Pretty simple! Instead of a third minigame, you’ll play a final Bowser challenge where you try to make the most noise. If you have the camera enabled, movement counts too.

Bowser and Bowser Jr. are not playable in this mode.

### Camera

If you picked the camera minigames options, you’ll play two of these three minigames:

Two of the following three minigames will be played during Bowser Live, and the selection will be determined via a roulette. The three minigames include:

| | Hitting It Rich It’s just how it looks. Use your fists to smash the Question Block. Team with the most coins wins. |
| --- | --- |
| | Goombalancing Act Use your head to catch Goombas falling from above. Each Goomba that stays balanced at the end of the minigame earns you a point. |
| | Talking Flower Says Follow the Talking Flower’s commands like “squat” and “stand.” Get the most commands correct to win. |

For your third and final game, Bowser will step up and put your team to the test with a voice and movement challenge. Make the most commotion to raise the meter, and the team that gets the most points wins a huge chunk of the total overall score.

### Microphone

Like the camera mode, two of the following three minigames will be played during Bowser Live, and the selection will be determined via a roulette. The three minigames include:

| | Bowser Chicken Work with your partner to yell “Go” to move your cart forward >Try to get as close as Bowser as you can without crossing over. |
| --- | --- |
| | Speak Up, Junior! Speak up to raise Bowser Jr. and collect the passing coins. The louder and longer you speak, the higher you’ll go |
| | Bowser Beats Clap to the beat of the music. Everyone works on the same track, so look out for your icon. |

Just like the camera mode, the final game will be a shout as loud as you can test.

## Carnival Coaster

Carnival Coaster is the second of four modes in Jamboree TV. This one requires you to play using mouse controls through your Joy-Con 2.

The premise is simple. Work together with two other players or four other players and ride the roller coaster through a series of rounds. Use the mouse controls to attack enemies that appear to add seconds to your time. Every time the coaster enters a pipe, a minigame is played to wrap up a round. How well you rank in the minigame determines how much time is added to the clock. This mode is very similar to River Survival from Super Mario Party.

There are five levels to pick from, each with varying amounts of rounds. We’ll add more information about each level soon.

Volcano Coaster

Sky-High Coaster

Carnival Coaster

## Mario Party

Mario Party is the third of four modes in Jamboree TV. It’s essentially the same mode from the original game but with two new rulesets and a new camera feature where players with their camera on will appear in game and have their live reactions front and center. Face icons will even adapt to certain events, like getting a Star or playing in specific minigames.

 

Frenzy Rules sets the turn count to 5 and gives players a boost with 50 coins, a Double Dice, and a Star right from the first turn. Tag-Team Rules splits four players into teams of two. There are a few baffling omissions from this version of Super Mario Party Jamboree. Pro Rules are not available, so you can’t play this ruleset with the resolution bump or the camera features. Minigame records are not recorded and Party Points aren’t saved either. 

### Frenzy Rules

In a series first, the main Mario Party mode can be played with a maximum of five turns — but this comes with a few rule changes. From the start, players recieve Double Dice, 50 coins, and one Star. A typical Last Five Turns event is added right from the start, but this time two events are randomly selected. As you would expect in the last five turns, duels are activated when landing on the same space as another player.

A shorter game means fewer bonus Stars, so only one will be awarded at the end of the game.

### Tag-Team Rules

In Tag Team Rules, partner up with another player and share your coins and Stars as you run around the board separately. You’ll start the game by rolling dice blocks, and whichever team rolls the highest combined roll gets to start first. From there, each team will alternate players until everyone has moved during the turn.

 

This mode gets a new item! The Together Dice allows you to roll your standard dice block, but it also brings your partner directly to your space and has them roll a second dice block. The combined roll determines how many spaces both you and your partner move, and the two of you will recieve Jamboree Buddy effects. That includes double items and double Stars! Once you complete your turn, your partner will return to their original space.

There’s a new space too. The Rally Space brings your partner directly to your location. Their arrival also gets you 5 coins, just like you’d get if you landed on a partner’s space anywhere else on the board. Your partner will stay on Rally Space once your turn ends!

## Free Play (List of Minigames)

Free Play is the fourth of four modes in Jamboree TV. It’s fairly straightforward. Pick and play minigames from throughout the other modes.

It’s nearly the same version of Free Play from the base game, but a few minigames are missing from the list. Any minigame from the Bowser Kaboom Squad, Koopathlon, or Rhythm Kitchen modes are not included.

There are 20 new minigames in total in Jamboree TV. Six of them are Bowser Live minigames, while the rest are used in Carnival Coaster and the main Mario Party mode. Each of the new 14 non-Bowser minigames can be played through three variations: Battle, Team of 2, and Team of 4. Battle allows two teams of two to face off against each other, while the other two variations have all players working together to score the best possible rank. Battle minigames are used in Mario Party while the team variations are used in Carnival Coaster. Shell Hockey is notably the only minigame not to have a Team of 4 variation.

### List of Jamboree TV Minigames

# Together Dice

| Together Dice | |
| --- | --- |
| | |
| Description | |
| Call teammate, roll 2 dice, and move total amount. Items, Stars, and space effects are doubled. | |
| Appears in | Super Mario Party Jamboree – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV (2025) |
| Effect | Brings teammate over to the player's space and allows both to move at the same time, moving the combined distance of two Dice Blocks. All board events are doubled. (Super Mario Party Jamboree – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV) |

The Together Dice is a special Dice Block in the Mario Party series introduced in Super Mario Party Jamboree – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV. 

The Together Dice only appears in Tag Team Rules in the Jamboree TV version of the Mario Party mode, replacing the Jamboree Buddies. It calls the player's teammate over to their space and both they and their teammate roll one of the two Dice Blocks. After rolling, the two rolls are combined and both the player and the teammate move together the combined distance. All board events that happen while this item is in use, such as buying items or getting a Star, will happen twice, similarly to the aforementioned Jamboree Buddies. After the turn is over, the teammate will return to their original space. It costs 20 coins at the Koopa Troopa Shop and only appears in the latter half of the game on every board, replacing one of the items that would be available at the shop otherwise. 

If both players roll the same number, they will receive 10 coins, similar to the result of rolling the same number with Double Dice.

# Overview trailer – Super Mario Party Jamboree Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV

As we found out in the Switch 2 Direct, Super Mario Party Jamboree is getting a paid upgrade later this year, exclusive to the new console! Titled Super Mario Party Jamboree Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV (what a mouthful), the upgrade expands the base game and adds brand-new features that take advantage of all the Switch 2 has to offer. 

An overview trailer was just released showcasing the upgrade you’ll be able to experience soon — l et’s take a look at what will be included! 

### Camera

- Using the Nintendo Switch 2 Camera, up to four players can appear on screen, letting you see real time reactions. 

### New rules

- Tag-Team Rules: Pair up with a partner, allowing you to play new minigames and discover new items exclusive to the mode.
- Frenzy Mode: five turns total, with each player starting with 50 coins, a Double Dice Block and a Star.

### New items

- Together Dice: Exclusive to Tag-Team Rules, this item warps your partner to your location and has you each roll a die, moving the total amount of spaces. If you land on a Star space, you’ll receive double the amount, but beware! You’ll also receive any negative effects on the way. 

### New Mode

- Bowser Live: By using the Camera, you are able to appear on stream, allowing you to use your full body to play minigames. Even if you don’t have a camera, there are minigames that utilize the microphone. 
- Carnival Coaster: Use mouse controls to shoot enemies as you traverse the coaster, entering minigames as you enter warp pipes. Winning minigames will give you more time on the coaster. 5 different courses available, with different difficulties. 

### New minigames

- Minigames exclusive to the Switch 2, using mouse controls, a more expressive rumble, and the microphone. 

- Able to be shared to up to 3 other systems, even if they don’t have the game. Players are limited to Mega Wiggler’s Tree Party. 

Super Mario Party Jamboree Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV will be available on July 24th, along with the upgrade pack for players who already own the game. 

### Written by Roberto Diaz

# Jamboree Buddy

| Jamboree Buddy | |
| --- | --- |
| Artwork of Mario with Bowser Jr. as his Jamboree Buddy, showcasing the latter's Jamboree Buddy ability. | |
| First appearance | Super Mario Party Jamboree (2024) |
| Latest appearance | Super Mario Party Jamboree – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV (2025) |

: “It looks like allies stick around for three turns. Pretty handy, huh? But watch out! If an opponent passes you, your ally will go with them. So keep your eyes peeled, and don't let anyone pass you!”
: — Toad, Super Mario Party Jamboree

Jamboree Buddies are characters who assist a character in Super Mario Party Jamboree, with 10 of the 22 playable characters having this role. When a character encounters a Jamboree Buddy on the board, a Showdown minigame linked to the Jamboree Buddy begins, wherein the character who activates it has a slight advantage at the start. If a tie occurs, the player who rolls the highest in the following "Tie-Break Dice" event earns the Jamboree Buddy. 

On boards, each Jamboree Buddy has their own unique ability and cause all board actions to occur twice, such as gaining or losing coins, purchasing items or Stars, and even Boos and Bowser Spaces. When obtained, the Jamboree Buddy leaves after two turns, meaning they are only around for three turns total. Similarly, if no character reaches the Jamboree Buddy within three turns, that Jamboree Buddy leaves. [1] An opponent can steal the Jamboree Buddy from the player who has them by passing them, making them their ally instead. [2] 

A Jamboree Buddy will only appear if they are not already one of the four board participants, so under normal circumstances a character cannot participate in their own Showdown minigame. In Free Play, Showdown Minigame Battle, online matchmaking, and Party-Planner Trek, if one of the player characters are a Jamboree Buddy, a monochrome imposter of that Jamboree Buddy will take their place in the respective Showdown minigame. 

In Jamboree TV, Jamboree Buddies will not appear in Tag Team Rules.

## Achievements [edit]

Each Jamboree Buddy has a corresponding achievement that the player unlocks by gaining them as an ally and using their ability for the first time:

- Luigi: Luigi's Chum

- Daisy: Daisy's Cheer Squad

- Waluigi: Team Waluigi
- Yoshi: Yoshi Fan
- Rosalina: Rosalina Admiration Brigade
- Donkey Kong: DK Crew
- Bowser Jr.: Bowser Jr.'s Accomplice

There is an unlockable "Bowser's Groupies" achievement if the player lands on a Bowser Space with a Jamboree Buddy.

- Much like the Ally mechanic in Super Mario Party: 

- Mario and Luigi do not have dialogue when approached, due to them being mostly silent protagonists. Instead, the Toad host speaks for them.

# How does Luigi affect your chance of rolling bigger numbers?

Tags: super-mario-party-jamboree

- Score: 6
- Views: 2375
- Answers: 1
- Answered: yes
- Asked by: Stevoisiak (48498 rep)
- Asked: 2024-11-08
- Site: gaming

## Question

When you get Luigi as a buddy in Super Mario Party Jamboree, the game says his ability is:

When you hit a dice you'll have an easier time rolling bigger numbers.

How exactly does Luigi's ability work when you roll a dice? Is it like a weighted dice? If so, how much more likely are you to roll higher numbers?

Screenshot courtesy of Alpharad

## Answers

### Answer by Pilzkopf (score: 8 [ACCEPTED])

After rolling all your dice on your turn Luigi will attempt to nudge the dice. If he succeeds the value of the dice is set to 10, else it stays the same as before.
If you rolled two or three dice in your turn and he succeeds all dice will change to a 10. You will thus also get the doubles / triples bonus coins.
The specific chance of the ability triggering is unclear but it seems to be around 33%.

Image source
